bull_case: $24.0B cash, a fully undrawn $7.5B revolver, only $2.25B debt principal due within 12 months and roughly $40.7B TTM OCF give Broadcom substantial self-funding capacity. Continued AI/software cash generation can absorb debt reduction, dividends and ordinary capex without survival financing.
bear_case: Gross debt is about $59.4B, binding purchase/other commitments total $130.8B, and AI XPV adds a maximum $29B backstop plus conditional customer-note exposure. A customer-led AI downturn could hit demand, working capital and contingent financing at the same time.
thesis: Broadcom's operating business is strongly self-funding, so refinancing or dilution is not currently a survival requirement. The constraint is off-balance and customer-financing exposure rather than near-term debt maturity. Binding commitments plus the XPV backstop are roughly 1.79x frozen TTM revenue, keeping the off-balance criterion at 55 despite otherwise strong liquidity.

evidence.claim: At 2026-08-02 Broadcom had $23.975B cash and a $7.5B unsecured revolver with no borrowings outstanding; only $2.252B of $61.079B debt principal was payable within 12 months.
evidence.source: User-supplied 10-Q filed 2026-09-10, Liquidity and Capital Resources / Note 6

evidence.claim: 9M FY2026 OCF was $32.950B; frozen TTM OCF is about $40.653B versus $59.419B carrying debt, while 9M net debt payments were $6.054B.
evidence.source: User-supplied 10-Q filed 2026-09-10 plus frozen company_context arithmetic

evidence.claim: Binding purchase commitments were $126.821B and other contractual commitments $3.941B at 2026-08-02, concentrated in FY2027 and FY2028.

AI XPV carried a maximum potential $29B lease backstop; fair value was not material and no amounts had been paid. The customer could under conditions issue up to $42B of convertible promissory notes to Broadcom, with none issued as of the quarter end.
Q3 diluted weighted-average shares were 4.887B versus 4.860B a year earlier, an increase of about 0.56%; 9M stock repurchases were $8.450B.
Broadcom sold $3.950B of receivables under non-recourse factoring arrangements during 9M FY2026, so reported OCF includes accelerated receivable monetization that should be monitored.

counterevidence: Purchase commitments are large but are partly associated with customer programs and should not be treated as equivalent to funded debt.
The $29B backstop is a maximum contingent amount, not a current liability; management reported immaterial fair value and no payments.
The $42B potential customer notes are conditional and had not been issued, so adding the full amount to current obligations would overstate present leverage.
Receivables factoring is non-recourse and does not by itself imply liquidity stress, although it can flatter operating cash conversion.
unknowns: The probability-weighted loss distribution and phase-by-phase funded amount of the $29B backstop are not disclosed.
The binding funding obligation, if any, associated with the up-to-$42B customer convertible-note capacity is unclear.
The fraction of $126.8B purchase commitments matched to non-cancellable customer RPO is not disclosed.
Debt maturity detail beyond the next 12 months was not reconstructed into a year-by-year stress table in this pass.
falsifiers: Liquidity score should fall if TTM OCF drops below $25B while net debt exceeds 2x TTM OCF.
Off-balance risk becomes severe if funded backstop/customer-note exposure plus binding commitments exceeds 2x TTM revenue without matched non-cancellable customer commitments.
Dilution veto must be reconsidered if diluted shares rise more than 3% y/y for four consecutive quarters despite repurchases.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Broadcom's own operations generate cash far above ordinary capex and near-term debt maturities, so the company does not require repeated external financing to operate. XPV financing supports customers and is routed to off-balance risk rather than this veto.
Q3 diluted shares increased only about 0.56% y/y while Broadcom repurchased $8.45B of stock in 9M. The 'excessive' element is not supported even though SBC remains material.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 파산 또는 영구손실 확률이 기대수익에 비해 지나치게 높음
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Cash plus undrawn revolver, strong OCF and only $2.252B principal due within 12 months refute a material near-term bankruptcy probability. Large AI commitments remain a scored tail risk, not evidence that business value is likely to be extinguished.

key_kpis.name: binding commitments + funded XPV exposure / TTM revenue

next_checks: Reconstruct debt maturities and fixed/floating interest burden by fiscal year.
Track actual XPV backstop funding, customer-note issuance and recoveries separately from headline AI revenue.
Adjust cash-conversion analysis for receivables factoring and working-capital timing.

subscores.rationale: Cash $23.975B, undrawn $7.5B revolver, roughly $40.7B TTM OCF and only $2.252B debt due within 12 months fit the 75 strong-liquidity anchor. The 90 anchor is excluded because Broadcom is net debt and has large contractual commitments.

Current internal cash generation can cover ordinary capex and near-term maturities even under a meaningful slowdown, fitting the 75 internal-cash-defense anchor. 90 is excluded because AI purchase commitments and XPV backstop exposure could become procyclical in a customer stress event.

Diluted shares rose about 0.56% y/y, mapping to the 0-3% row score of 55. Binding purchase commitments + other contractual commitments + maximum backstop are about $159.8B, roughly 1.79x frozen TTM revenue $89.1B, also mapping to 55; policy takes the lower axis. The conditional $42B customer-note capacity is excluded from the deterministic ratio because no notes were issued and the binding funding obligation is unclear.

uncertainties.rationale: Gross debt is manageable today, but large future purchase commitments create a substantial forward cash requirement not captured by near-term debt alone.
AI customer default could hit demand, working capital and backstop exposure at the same time.
If the conditional $42B note capacity becomes a binding funded obligation, off-balance exposure would move above the 2x-revenue severe-risk row.
